Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

plot noun and verb

a secret plan against someone

also conspiracy, conspire, conspirator, conspirators, plotter, plot against, hatch a plot, scheme

classical

Caes. BG 1.2.1: conjūrātiōnem nōbilitātis fēcit
Cic. Off. 3.44
Sall. C. 17.1 (Lewis & Short)

conjūrātiō, conjūrātiōnis f.

noun, third declension · Declension on Wiktionary

a conspiracy, a plot

A plot sworn to by several, mostly against the state or its rulers; conjūrātiōnem facere, to form a plot. First a swearing together, and so any league: Laches in Terence complains of the conjūrātiō of all women (Ter. Hec. 198, Lewis & Short, at Hec. 2.1.1). The plotters are conjūrātī.

Other words

  • conjūrō, conjūrāre, conjūrāvī, conjūrātum — to plot, to conspire

    verb, first conjugation, intransitive · also used · classical · Cic. Sull. 70: contrā rem pūblicam (Lewis & Short); Caes. BG 2.3: contrā populum Rōmānum (Lewis & Short) · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    To swear together; in a bad sense, very often, to conspire, with contrā, in or ut.

  • īnsidiae, īnsidiārum f. pl. — a plot, a trap laid for someone

    noun, first declension, plural · also used · classical · Cic. Rosc. Am. 26: īnsidiās parāre (Lewis & Short); Cic. Q. Fr. 2.3.4: vītae alicujus īnsidiās facere (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

    First an ambush; then any plot or trap laid for one person, by one or by many: īnsidiās facere, parāre, struere alicui, to plot against someone.

  • mōlior, mōlīrī, mōlītus sum — to work at, to scheme, to plot

    verb, fourth conjugation, deponent · also used · classical · Cic. Rep. 2.60: dē occupandō rēgnō mōliēns (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. revolutionary: nova mōlīrī · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    To set something heavy in motion, and so to work hard at, to contrive; with īnsidiās, fugam, nova (revolution), to plot it. Not a word for plotting by itself.

Examples

  • Is … rēgnī cupiditāte inductus conjūrātiōnem nōbilitātis fēcit

    He, led on by desire for the throne, formed a plot among the noblesCaes. BG 1.2.1

  • nam sī omnia facienda sint, quae amīcī velint, nōn amīcitiae tālēs, sed conjūrātiōnēs putandae sint

    for if we must do everything our friends want, such ties should be called conspiracies, not friendshipsCic. Off. 3.44

See also plot, enemy, war.
